newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge limits punitive claims on tobacco companies.
newsitem.headline: Florida judge limits punitive claims on tobacco companies.

text.p: A judge in Florida's Medicaid lawsuit against the tobacco industry Tuesday sharply limited the amount of punitive damages that may be sought in the case.

The judge, Harold Cohen of the Palm Beach County Circuit Court, restricted punitive damages, but let let stand claims for triple damages on alleged racketeering by the tobacco companies being sued by Florida for taxpayer money spent on treating sick smokers.
In addition, Cohen said Florida could pursue limited additional damages if it can prove fraud by tobacco companies through advertising or false claims made after 1982.
Before Cohen's ruling, Florida had been arguing it was entitled to punitive damages as well as recovering the money spent treating smokers through its Medicaid program.

But Cohen said a Florida law passed in 1994 that is the main vehicle for Florida's lawsuit did not allow for punitive damages but only actual damages. The fraud claims are being brought under a separate law, Cohen said.

Florida can also pursue triple damages if it wins in the scheduled August trial for alleged racketeering under still another Florida law, the judge ruled. Florida claims the tobacco companies conspired to hide the dangers of smoking from Americans and sold them dangerous products.
